sections.title: Order Book & New Orders
sections.subtitle: The lead indicator for an EPC conglomerate: backlog and inflow run 1-3 years ahead of revenue

charts.title: Order Book & New Order Inflow
charts.annotation: Orders received is disclosed by L&T only half-yearly and at FY, not every quarter, so this chart is FY-only; order book is the point-in-time backlog at each fiscal year-end (L&T reports it quarterly, shown here on the same FY-only axis for comparability).

charts.title: Gross Profit, Operating Income & Net Income
Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

series.label: Cash only (excl. investments & other bank balances)

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Larsen & Toubro Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted). Cash only is the subset of cash & equivalents held as bank balances and deposits, excluding current investments and other bank balances (margin money, unpaid-dividend escrow, etc.).

For Larsen & Toubro Limited: most of L&T's reported cash & equivalents sits in current investments rather than bank cash, and consolidated debt is dominated by the L&T Finance NBFC borrowing book, not the core EPC business -- the standalone net-debt/equity (~0.33x) the company quotes is far lower than the group ratio here.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Gap between cash & equivalents and cash only -- a widening gap means more of the balance is parked in investments, not bank cash
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Larsen & Toubro Limited: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Larsen & Toubro Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Larsen & Toubro Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Larsen & Toubro Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Larsen & Toubro Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

orderBook.title: Order book and new order inflow
orderBook.content:
The order book is the unexecuted value of signed contracts at a point in time -- the backlog L&T has already won but not yet billed. Orders received is new business signed during the period (half-year or full year). Book-to-bill is orders received divided by revenue in the same period: above 1x, the backlog is growing faster than it is being converted to revenue.

For Larsen & Toubro Limited: as a fixed-price EPC contractor, L&T's order book is the best 1-3 year forward indicator of revenue -- far more useful than any single quarter's results, which are driven by execution milestones on contracts won years earlier. Management's Lakshya 2031 plan targets 10-12% order-inflow CAGR against a 12-15% revenue CAGR.

What to watch:

  • Order-inflow growth decelerating ahead of a revenue slowdown
  • Book-to-bill trending below 1x for several periods in a row
  • Concentration of new orders in lower-margin segments (e.g. WET/water projects) or in the GCC, where execution and geopolitical risk run higher

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Larsen & Toubro Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Larsen & Toubro Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Larsen & Toubro Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
